reason: The only available action should start seawater moving into the fractured seafloor.
expectation: I expect seawater to enter the fractures and move toward hot rock, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Seawater has entered the crust, so the next step is to heat it.
reaction: The start of a circulation loop is clear and satisfying.
reason: Heating the infiltrating seawater should advance the vent circulation; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the seawater to heat up in contact with the rock, possibly changing its chemistry.

effect: The seawater is now heated within the crust; pressure keeps the hot fluid below the surface.
reaction: The role of pressure is a useful detail.
reason: The only offered combination brings the heated water into contact with changing basalt, advancing the circulation loop.
expectation: I expect water–rock reactions to alter the fluid and possibly add dissolved minerals.

effect: The heated water has exchanged dissolved material with rock; it can now follow fractures back toward the sea.
reaction: The qualification that vent fluids vary is useful.
reason: The only offered combination may let the mineral-bearing fluid rise through the seafloor fractures.
expectation: I expect the hydrothermal fluid to emerge into the sea, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The fluid is rising through a separate return path, driven by buoyancy and pressure differences.
reaction: The distinction between entry and return paths makes the circulation clearer.
reason: Mixing the hot fluid with cooler seawater may precipitate minerals and build the vent deposit.
expectation: I expect cooling to cause some dissolved minerals to form solids, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Returning the fluid to the sea also advances a goal, but I want to explore the cooling and deposit first.

effect: Cooling and mixing precipitated minerals, providing material for a vent deposit.
reaction: It is satisfying to see dissolved material become solid, with the composition left conditional.
reason: Combining the precipitating minerals with the fractures should build the deposit around the vent.
expectation: I expect mineral solids to accumulate around a seafloor vent, though the exact structure is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Returning hot fluid to the sea also serves a goal, but I want to finish the deposit first.

effect: Repeated precipitation built a modest vent deposit, completing that goal; the remaining goal is to return heated water to the sea.
reaction: The distinction between a modest deposit and a towering chimney is useful.
reason: The only offered combination returns the hot fluid to the sea.
expectation: I expect the heated fluid to enter the early sea and complete the circulation goal.

effect: The hot fluid returned to the sea as a hydrothermal plume, completing the circulation goal and the chapter.
reaction: The reminder that a visible plume is not necessarily smoke or evidence of life was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mixing hot fluid with cooler seawater made precipitation tangible and connected dissolved material to the vent deposit.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial sequence was clear but largely mechanical, with only one combination offered at each step.

surprise.text: The fluid could enter through one part of the fractured system and return through another, clarifying the circulation loop.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though using open fractures to build the deposit felt somewhat abstract.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow more natural processes presented with the same useful qualifications, although I would prefer more meaningful choices.
